title: Iowa band member taken off life support, dies after collapsing in heat at Kinnick Stadium
content:
A third-year University of Iowa band member died Tuesday morning, three days after suffering a heart attack in the stifling heat at Kinnick Stadium on Saturday, according to a news release from the university’s band and music departments.

Derek Phillips, who led the Hawkeye Marching Band’s mellophone section, was taken off life support Monday. In a statement on Instagram, Phillips’ family wrote, “Despite the extraordinary efforts of the ICU team at the University of Iowa Hospital, the damage to his brain was too severe, and we have made the heartbreaking decision to remove life support.”

Iowa football coach Kirk Ferentz said he was “heartbroken” to learn about Phillips’ death.

“On behalf of everybody associated with our program, we just want to offer our thoughts, our condolences to his family, his friends and all the people he impacted, certainly, in his life,” said Ferentz, who opened his Tuesday news conference discussing Phillips. “It’s just a really, really, very, very sad thing.”

Heat-related issues were prevalent at stadiums around the country Saturday, and particularly in Iowa City, where the temperature reached 92 degrees and the heat index soared to at least 105 degrees with limited cloud cover. For the first time, the Hawkeye Marching Band did not perform at halftime because of excessive heat.

Phillips, a Western Dubuque (Iowa) High graduate, performed and traveled with the band, and he also participated in drama.

“Derek brought so much light, humor and kindness into this world,” his family wrote. “He was a phenomenal musician — whether he was playing jazz, singing his heart out, or marching under the lights, music was the language of his soul. He just had the absolute summer of his life touring in drum and bugle corps. We are so grateful for that experience.”

In a statement, the directors of the Hawkeye Marching Band and School of Music wrote Wolfe was “the kind of friend, student, and musician that represents the very best of what it means to be a Hawkeye.”

“This Saturday, and for the rest of our season, the Hawkeye Marching Band and School of Music will honor Derek’s memory, and we will communicate those details as they take shape,” the statement read.

Counselors were made available to university students. The Hawkeye Marching Band is set to perform Saturday as part of the Iowa-Iowa State football game at Kinnick Stadium.

In a statement, the university wrote: “The entire Hawkeye Marching Band family is thinking of Derek Phillips and his loved ones. We are grateful to his parents for providing regular updates to the students who love Derek. This is heartbreaking for everyone who cares for him. The university is in close contact and is offering support.”
